source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary

source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 31 — TREES OF MASTIC, ALOES, AND NARD — Aramaic 4Q206 1 xxi-xxii partial; Greek Akhmim 31:1-3 complete; Ge'ez full.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο ὄρος ἐν ᾧ δένδρα, καὶ ἐξέρρει ὕδωρ ἐξ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξήρχετο ὥσπερ νέκταρ καλούμενον σαραρά καὶ γαλβανῆ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon allo oros en hō dendra, kai exerrei hydōr ex autou, kai exērcheto hōsper nektar kaloumenon sarara kai galbanē.
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ ካልአ፡ ደብረ፡ ዘቦቱ፡ ዕፀወ፡ ወይውኅዝ፡ ማይ፡ እምኔሁ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ከመ፡ ቤዘር፡ ዘይሰመይ፡ ሰረራ፡ ወጋልባን፡
verses.notes: **Sarara and galbanē** — sarara is a Semitic transliteration (likely a tree-gum name); galbanē is Greek galbanum (Exod 30:34 — ingredient of incense). The mountain with aromatic-gum-bearing trees.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐπάνω τούτου τοῦ ὄρους εἶδον ἄλλο ὄρος, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ δένδρα ἀλόης ἦν, καὶ τὰ δένδρα πεπληρωμένα ὁμοία στακτῇ τῇ σκληροτέρᾳ.
verses.translit: Kai epanō toutou tou orous eidon allo oros, kai en autō dendra aloēs ēn, kai ta dendra peplērōmena homoia staktē tē sklēroterā.
verses.text_geez: ወመልዕልተ፡ ዝደብር፡ ርእኩ፡ ካልአ፡ ደብረ፡ ወውስቴቱ፡ ዕፀወ፡ ጻበል፡ ሀለዉ፡ ወዕፀው፡ ምሉዓነ፡ ይመስሉ፡ ቅንፍ፡ ጽኑዐ፡
verses.notes: **Aloe trees on the higher mountain.** Cf. Ps 45:8 (myrrh, aloes, cassia on royal garments); John 19:39 (Nicodemus brings myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial); Prov 7:17.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ὅταν τις τρίψῃ αὐτὰ τῶν δένδρων τούτων ἀπεκπνεῖ ἐκείνη ἡ ὀσμὴ πάντων εὐωδέστερον.
verses.translit: Kai hotan tis tripsē auta tōn dendrōn toutōn apekpnei ekeinē hē osmē pantōn euōdesteron.
verses.text_geez: ወሶበ፡ የሐስስ፡ መኑሂ፡ እምነ፡ እማንቱ፡ ዕፀው፡ ይነፍሥ፡ ውእቱ፡ ሕብር፡ ዘይጥዕም፡ እምኵሉ፡
verses.notes: When the trees are bruised, their fragrance exceeds all others. Paradisiacal-fragrance motif.
